text: Dina Nath Walli (1908–2006), also known by his pen name Almast Kashmiri, was an Indian watercolour artist and poet from Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley. He was a key figure in the modern art movement in Jammu and Kashmir and is recognized for painting everyday scenes of Kashmir. Born in 1906 in the Badyar Bala neighborhood of Srinagar, within the then princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, part of British India, he belonged to a Kashmiri Pandit family; his father passed away when he was very young. He received his early education in Srinagar and later completed a three-year course at Amar Singh Technical Institute, Srinagar, before moving to Calcutta in the Bengal Presidency in 1930 for further artistic training, where he studied various art forms under Percy Brown, the principal of the Government College of Art & Craft at the University of Calcutta. In 1936, he returned to Srinagar and focused on landscape painting in watercolours. He was awarded gold medals by the government of Kashmir in 1939 and received a highly commended medal from the Academy of Fine Arts, Calcutta in 1940. He also produced an album containing 12 paintings. Under the pen name Almast Kashmiri, his emphasis on realistic art and people's poetry is evident in his two poetry collections: Bala Yapair (This side of Mountains, 1955) and Sahaavukh Posh (Desert Flowers, 1981).
